newsitem.title: India: Indian gold prices down despite overseas gains.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold prices down despite overseas gains.

text.p: ** Indian gold prices fall at the close amid sluggish
seasonal buying and despite overseas gains
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) end 100 rupees
** Silver (.999) eases by 10 rupees at 6,875 rupees per kg

Indian 24 carat gold prices on Tuesday fell by 10 rupees at 4,760 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,770 rupees amid sluggish seasonal buying which prompted light profit-taking, dealers said.
Even an uptrend in the world market failed to cheer local sentiments. Gold was up by five rupees per 10 grammes on Monday.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) closed 100 rupees lower at 55,700 rupees after gaining 100 rupees on Monday. They were down by 300 rupees during last week.

Silver (.999) closed 10 rupees lower at 6,875 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,885 rupees amid fresh arrivals. Sluggish industrial demand prompted unloading by stockists despite reports of an uptrend in the world market. Silver was up by 10 rupees per kg on Monday.
"Overall sentiments at the close remained subdued for both the precious metals but looking at the uptrend in the world market, local prices may bounce back," one broker added. ($1=35.80 rupees)
